correlation_mechanism: High furnace reheat temperature (1265°C) combined with elevated residual copper (0.32 wt% Cu) promotes liquid copper grain boundary penetration (hot shortness). High roll campaign tonnage (1850 t) compounds surface checking via fire-cracked roll wear.

Severe total oxygen excursion (38 ppm) and high soluble aluminum (0.045 wt%) indicate excessive secondary reoxidation and Al2O3 cluster entrapment, generating linear stringer inclusions under rolling elongation.

High roll campaign tonnage (2100 t) approaching work layer fatigue limit triggered work roll peeling (band shelling) on finishing stand F2, transferring compressed scab-like patches onto the strip surface.

Critical descaling header pressure drop (138 bar vs nominal 190+ bar) failed to dislodge secondary scale. High silicon (0.48 wt%) facilitated fayalite root anchoring, producing severe indentations that pickled out as pitted surface cavities.

Extended furnace soak at 1280°C combined with high silicon content (0.55 wt% Si) generated tenacious fayalite (Fe2SiO4) eutectic scale layers. Sub-nominal descaling pressure (142 bar) resulted in embedded rolled-in scale streaks.

Excessive strip threading velocity (1080 m/min) caused severe side guide chatter and strip tracking oscillation, pinching strip shoulders against stationary guide aprons and imparting longitudinal scratches.
